newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - S.Africa Q3 gold mine profit seen dulled.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - S.Africa Q3 gold mine profit seen dulled.

text.p: Annual wage increases and a sluggish gold price are likely to impede third quarter earnings growth for South African gold mines, analysts said on Thursday.
Analysts polled by Reuters said after-capex income may rise between five and eight percent -- a substantial downsizing from the 10 to 15 percent forecast at the end of the June quarter.

"Around about eight (percent increase) across the board. The wage increase will come through mainly in this quarter and the gold price has not done that much lately," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
Gengold Ltd and Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd kick off third quarter reporting on Monday.
The 1996/7 wage increase of five to 10.4 percent agreed last month was backdated to July and so the three months to end-September carry the impact of this cost to the industry.
Furthermore, while a rand gold price sitting comfortably above 1,700 rand per ounce is nothing to sneeze at it offers no exciting new riches to the September quarter's earnings.
The rand gold price was last at 1,737.35 rand per ounce and the last bullion price was $381.50 per ounce.

"After capex earnings available to pay out would be about 720 to 740 million rand for this quarter, compared to the 686 million rand last quarter," said Nick Goodwin, analyst at Fedsure Asset Management.

"Between five and eight percent up, which is actually not that good. There's nothing new that can help the mines. We're getting a slowing down and next quarter earnings could be lower because the gold price is not really going anywhere," he added.

The rand's loss of a quarter of its value since mid-February may have sparked the highest ever rand gold price, but inflationary costs would soon start to come through, knocking the labour and capital intensive mining industry, analysts said.
The rand was last bid at 4.5515 against the dollar.
Analysts said the industry -- suffering from declining productivity -- could look forward to a very slight increase in gold output in the third quarter due to fewer holidays.

But they added that recent labour unrest which halted production at some of the larger mines, including Kloof Gold Mining Co Ltd and Driefontein Consolidated Ltd, could take its toll on overall industry production.
"I'd say that after last quarter's 119 tonnes, we could have about 123 tonnes in the third quarter. A slight improvement because there were fewer holidays," Goodwin said.

"Production will be pretty even. The only thing that will affect it is how much Dries and Kloof have been knocked down due to violence. We might actually see an industry decline because of those two big ones," said another analyst.
Analysts said Driefontein, having lost production to underground fires last quarter, was taking a bashing that gave no hints of letting up in the near future.
Driefontein produced 11,680.6 kg of gold in the second quarter, compared to 12,977.4 kg in the first quarter.

Improved production for the industry as a whole was in sight but it would take at least two years to really improve, analysts said. Total gold output for 1996 was seen falling to a 40-year low of just 500 tonnes.
Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd's stable of mines was seen putting on a good show in the September quarter with Buffelsfontein Gold Mining Co Ltd shining.
Gengold was also seen staging a dazzling performance, while Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd and JCI Ltd were seen holding their own.
Mines hedged less in the September quarter due to the better gold price received, analysts said.
The average gold price for the industry was likely to be about 1,700 rand per ounce compared to 1,642 rand previously.
Costs for the third quarter would average about 1,320 rand per ounce compared to about 1,286 rand in the second quarter.
-- Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
